messages:
sam_infra: heads-up — I pulled gpu-node-12 out of rotation after two Xid 31s during the nightly compact. It passed quick smoke but flaked under the longer run. Thinking we should run the updated preflight validation before returning it to the pool.

anya: OK — can you paste the dmesg excerpt and ECC counters? last time ECC corrected spikes showed up ~30m before Xids. Also which image/kernel?

sam_infra: kernel 6.1.0-rc, driver 550.66 (repro on the same driver locally). dmesg excerpt below (trimmed):
```
[ 2456.123456] NVRM: Xid (GPU 0000:81:00): 31, pid=22456, Graphics Exception
[ 2456.123478] NVRM:  R0: 0x00000000 R1: 0x00000000 R2: 0x00000000 R3: 0x00000000
[ 2460.567890] nvidia: GPU 0: ECC errors corrected: 12  (mmu ecc corrected)
```
Also ran: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERFORMANCE` — ECC shows 12 corrected, 0 uncorrected.

ben: thanks. Proposal for a formal preflight suite (what we'll run before rejoin):
- quick memtest (memtest86-like) 2h
- STRESS-GPU (shader+mem) 12–24h continuous, collecting dmesg and nvlink stats
- thermal cycling: 6 cycles (idle->full->cooldown) over 6h to exercise thermal boundaries
- 1h production-like inference run using the same model profile that saw failures, with KV cache enabled

Pass criteria:
- zero Xid >= 31 during the STRESS-GPU window
- corrected ECC deltas <= 5 during entire suite (if >5, hold for longer soak)
- no kernel oops or PCI resets
- telemetry: collect /var/log/kern.log, `nvidia-bug-report.sh`, and `/sys/module/nvidia/parameters/*` where relevant

Suggested command to start (WIP):
```bash
soakctl start --node gpu-node-12 --suite preflight-v2 --duration 24h 
# artifacts will be uploaded to s3://redwood-soak-artifacts/soak-1790123345/
```

jen: one operational note — gate for returning nodes: if the suite passes, node goes into a 72h probation mode in canary pool (traffic limited to <5% until stable). If it fails at any point, auto-create an RMA ticket with vendor logs attached.

anya: question on the ECC threshold: why <=5? sounds tight vs current 12 corrected.

ben: 5 is a compromise — we saw historical false positives up to ~8 in warm racks but those never progressed to Xid. If corrected ECC is between 6–12 and no Xids, we do extended 48h soak in isolated pool. If >12 or any Xid, escalate to RMA.

sam_infra: vendor guidance (email) said intermittent Xid 31 often indicates memory substrate issues; if we can reproduce deterministically under stress -> RMA. If only occasional in long-run, sometimes thermal/power cycling fixes. Hence the thermal cycling step.

ci-bot: started soak job `soak-1790123345` on gpu-node-12: https://ci.redwood.ai/soaks/soak-1790123345 — logs streaming. :rocket:

jen: nice — please update the ticket template used for RMA to include the soak run id, timestamps, driver/kernel versions, and the `nvidia-bug-report.sh` tarball. Also include `lspci -vvv` output.

sam_infra: will do. Also thinking about cost — running 24h soak on a spare pool is ~22 GPU-hours (we spin up 2 GPUs for staging), roughly $X/day. ben: can we shift soak runs to preemptible/spot capacity when we don't need immediate results?

ben: yes for non-urgent rechecks. For nodes with potential warranty/RMA we prefer dedicated test hosts to avoid preemptions interfering with repro. For background validation we can use spot.

anya: one more: can we add a short script to parse kernel logs and auto-flag Xid patterns and ECC deltas, then annotate the soak job result with tags `XID`/`ECC_HIGH`/`PASS`? that will speed triage.

sam_infra: good idea — I'll add a small parser that emits a JSON summary (run id, xids_found, ecc_delta, top-3 stack frames) and uploads it to artifacts. CI can then add labels automatically.

jen: great. Sounding like an actionable plan. Sam — kick it off tonight and ping when the job completes or if it repros quickly.

sam_infra: starting tonight. run id soak-1790123345. will @mention this thread on completion.

ci-bot: soak-1790123345 is still running — currently 3h elapsed, no new Xids, ECC corrected delta=0.

ben: awesome. thanks team. we should write this up as a short playbook (one-pager) and add it to ops runbooks so oncall can follow the same flow.

anya: agree — I'll draft the playbook after we have full run artifacts.

sam_infra: closing for now — will reopen thread if anything changes. thanks all.
